issues.sourceClaim: The introduction broadly says AI models can adapt to unknown payloads without stating a data/update mechanism.
issues.qualification: Learning capability does not automatically update fixed weights when payload changes.

issues.sourceClaim: The M11 equation prints2m1l1l2cos(q2), whereas the depicted point-tip-mass model and code require2m2l1l2cos(q2).
issues.qualification: The distal mass velocity contains both link contributions, so its kinetic-energy cross term is proportional to m2.

issues.sourceClaim: The p1755 cross coefficient differs from the code and tip-mass derivation.
The dataset description broadly calls random joint-coordinate samples uniform workspace coverage; the printed code samples joint variables independently.
issues.qualification: A nonlinear kinematic map changes spatial density, and unrelated state tuples are not an integrated motion.

issues.sourceClaim: The adjacent RMSE graphic omits the mean over samples, while the code correctly uses np.sqrt(np.mean(error**2)).
issues.qualification: For one error, √(e²)=|e|. Dataset RMSE requires an explicit mean over samples.

issues.sourceClaim: The slide’s final only-q-input statement is overbroad if applied to the full torque predictor rather than its configuration subnetworks.
issues.qualification: Configuration determines the learned energy functions, while kinetic and acceleration terms still depend on motion.

issues.sourceClaim: The equation page calls q̇ᵀHq̇ kinetic energy without the physical factor one-half; its −½∇T term is consistent only when T denotes twice physical kinetic energy.
issues.qualification: The displayed torque can be consistent with the doubled definition, while the kinetic-energy label is inaccurate.

issues.sourceClaim: Unlike p1764, the p1765 flowchart includes one-half inside T and again before its gradient, creating a factor-of-two error.
issues.qualification: The one-half is already included in T, so halving its gradient again is erroneous.

issues.sourceClaim: The p1765 half-gradient defect would give 14 rather than 12 for this added test.
issues.qualification: The four terms are 6, 8, −4 and 2, which sum to 12.

issues.sourceClaim: The example frames the smaller dataset as improved sample efficiency; its figures alone do not establish a universal tenfold guarantee or a fully controlled comparison.
issues.qualification: Architecture, training, seeds and evaluation conditions must be controlled before generalizing the comparison.

issues.sourceClaim: The training snippet instantiates DeLaN2R without providing its class definition, so the excerpt alone is not executable. No missing class or pretrained result is invented.
issues.qualification: The architecture constructor is called, but its class definition is absent from these pages.

issues.sourceClaim: The summary’s energy-conservation wording needs an unforced or zero-net-power qualification; powered or dissipative motion is not generally constant-energy.
issues.qualification: The learned conservative structure yields a work–energy balance; actuator work can change total energy.
